deep.reconstruction: This page has no mathematics: no formulas, derivations or computations. It is the start of a German letter draft, written quickly in pencil with corrections, broken off at the cut bottom edge. My reading, with uncertain words marked: 'Hochgeschätzter Herr Professor. [a crossed-out word, perhaps 'Vater', after a separator] / Vor allen Dingen [crossed out: 'drängt es mich'] muß ich, vor dem [Vorwurf?] [schützen?] ... wie wenig ich in der [interlinear: 'ausgesprochen'?] ... [Verpflichtungen?] gegen Sie [erfüllten? 'verflossenen'?] Monate ... [Bitten/Erbitten?], und daß [ich ihn] selb[st] nicht zu zürnen [?] und den Grund davon nicht in meiner Trägheit zum Briefschreiben, mit der ich von jeher zu kämpfen gehabt habe, [crossed out: 'zu suchen'], sondern in meinem [unbefriedigenden?] Gesundheitszustande zu suchen. Ohne die eine ... [cut off]'. In substance, Riemann apologises to an unnamed professor for a long silence or delay. He says the cause is not his lifelong reluctance to write letters but his poor health. This fits his last years (about 1862–1866), when tuberculosis took him to Italy. The bundle 'R.Ohr' contains material on the mechanics of the ear. The previous page is prose on method in physiology, and the next page lists small measurements in millimetres, apparently anatomical dimensions of parts of the ear. That context suggests a professional correspondent connected with the ear work. Jakob Henle is a plausible addressee, since he published Riemann's posthumous fragment 'Mechanik des Ohres' (1867). This is only a conjecture; the page names no one. No derivation exists to reconstruct.
